beginnings: A bowl to eat from and bricks to build with—not bad for four beginnings. Now we need something worth putting in that bowl.
supper: Flatbread and juice: a proper first supper. Take your time; we can look for somewhere to rest before the next stretch of river.
shelter: Daylight through the window, and a mat for the night: thank you, the cottage feels like a home now. The brook is just beyond the orchard.
crossing: A bridge for our feet, a cart for our loads, and a map for the next traveller. Downstream, the miller has been watching that same water go to waste.
mill: You could grind a handful before; now the village has a mill to do the work. Take that flour sack to the baker—she has a lighter loaf in mind.
bakery: There it is: a loaf with air in its crumb, and a basket for the road. The orchard keeper has been wondering how to save a little summer for the gathering.
orchard: Preserves under a lid and cider in a bottle. We can bring something of this orchard to the gathering without asking the fruit to stay ripe forever.
pottery: A smooth bowl and a table made for many suppers. Useful things can be beautiful, too. Our neighbours at the quarry could use a little of your ingenuity.
workshop: A pickaxe for hard ground and a chest to keep our tools together. Leave them within reach of the next pair of hands; there is wider water ahead.
ferry: A landing, a sailboat, and another stretch added to the map. The river is beginning to join our villages instead of keeping them apart.
harbour: A light above the water, a buoy below it, and a harbour marked on the map. Now let us think about the people those boats will bring.
garden: The climbing plants have support, and the tender ones have shelter. We have made them a good beginning; those uphill beds still need water.
waterworks: Water reaches the garden without another climb with a bucket. That leaves more hands free to prepare a welcome for our guests.
weavers: A banner to find us by and a canopy to gather beneath—it looks like a welcome. Now we ought to send the invitation.
letters: The invitations are printed and the mailboat is ready. We have something to tell our neighbours—and soon we will need something for them to hear.
music: A flute, a drum, and a place for the players. That is the beginning of a fine gathering. Leave a little room for the storyteller.
theatre: A little theatre for moving stories, and a picture book for keeping them. There are other stories nearby, too—even in a drop from the pond.
optics: A pond sample and the means to look closely. We need not travel far to find something unfamiliar; let us look at the plants along this same river.
botany: Specimens and drawings, together in a flora we can share. A traveller can compare a leaf with the page instead of relying on our memories.
weather: We have a record of wind and rain, not just a guess at the sky. I will keep it with our preparations; the shore cook is planning the crossing meals.
saltshore: Smoked fish and a jar of pickles: provisions for a boat without a hearth. The guests on shore will need looking after as well.
cleanwater: The washstand and covered water urn are ready. A welcome is more than decoration; it is noticing what people will need when they arrive.
stores: Room for grain, and dried fruit put away in its crock. We can celebrate the season without forgetting the one that follows it.
lanterns: A light that can float and a lamp for the watch. Keep the floating lantern for our sheltered landing; first, let us agree when everyone should arrive.
timekeeping: A timetable for the boats and a bell to call us together. The last visitors will come after dark; the watcher has been studying their route.
stars: River landmarks and stars on one navigation chart, with a steady telescope beside it. We can leave the next traveller something better than vague directions.
gallery: A mosaic on display and a catalogue to carry away. Our gathering has things to look at as well as things to eat; the kitchen is nearly ready for us.
washday: Soap at the washstand, where the cooks can use it. Now we can turn from preparing the kitchen to preparing the meal.
kitchen: The stove is ready, with porridge and fruit compote for the early arrivals. Bring the gathering to the table; we have been preparing for this together.
gathering: The table is laid, the atlas is finished, and a lantern floats at our landing. From four beginnings, a river full of things to share. Come and sit with us.
